title: Library API in Express
idea: The library API exposes borrow, return, renew and reserve as REST endpoints, with controllers for HTTP, a service for rules and transactions, and a repository for SQL.

analogy.text: A library's front window, back office and stacks. The window takes forms, the office applies rules, the stacks hold the books.
analogy.breaks: Here all three run in one process and one transaction.

points: Controllers parse headers and bodies with zod and never write SQL.
The service runs each use case in one transaction and throws domain errors.
Borrow takes an Idempotency-Key, so a retried click returns the same loan.
One error middleware maps zod, domain and Postgres errors to HTTP codes.

code.title: Layered Express app
code.caption: Repository, service, controllers and error mapping in one file on a real PostgreSQL. X-Member-Id stands in for real authentication.

walk.text: Demo schema: one copy, one waiting reservation, and a unique key per member for idempotency.
A fixed demo clock, a domain error type, and `tx` for one transaction per call.
Repository: find a loan by key, lock a free copy, update it, insert the loan.
Close the open loan with its fine, then mark the oldest reservation READY.
Service: replay by key, else lock and lend; return hands the copy to the queue.
Controllers validate and call the service. Express 5 forwards async throws to the one error middleware.
Happy path, replay, conflict, bad body, a late return and a repeated return.

pitfalls: Do not put SQL in controllers; keep HTTP, rules and queries in separate layers.
Scope the Idempotency-Key per member, or two members can collide on one key.
Do not return 500 for a known rule; map each domain error to 404 or 409.

quiz.q: What status does the second POST /loans with key k-1 print?
quiz.why: The service finds a loan stored under M-1 and k-1 and returns it without touching copies. The controller marks a replay with 200.

takeaway: Controllers speak HTTP, services own rules and transactions, repositories own SQL.
